badBarLengths: Bar lengths are whole percentages from 0 to 100, shortest at or below longest
badCount: Enter how many values, as a whole number of at least 1
badDuplicateRange: Enter a range like A1:A20, or separate areas like (A1:A20,C1:C20)
badRange: Enter a range like B2:B20, a table column like Sales[Amount], or separate areas like B2:B20,D2:D20
badThresholds: Thresholds are percentages from 0 to 100, low at or below high
bar.negativeSameBorder: Use positive border color for negative values
bar.negativeSameFill: Use positive fill color for negative values
barHint: Bars grow from zero (or from the lowest value when there are negatives) to the largest value in the range.
barOnly: Show the bar only, not the value
barThresholdHint: Thresholds accept numbers or formulas. Formulas use fixed sheet references; leave them blank to use the formatted range’s minimum and maximum.
duplicateHint: The ranges used to find duplicates or unique values. For separate areas, use (A1:A20,C1:C20). These ranges can differ from the cells being formatted.
formulaHint: Written for the top-left cell of the first area; relative references move with each cell, e.g. =$C2>B2 or =ISBLANK(A2).
iconOnly: Show the icon only, not the value
missingSheet: One of these ranges refers to a sheet that does not exist
moveDownTip: Move down (later rules give way to earlier ones)
moveUpTip: Move up (earlier rules win where they overlap)
noRules: No rules on this sheet yet.
notChanged: The rule could not be changed. Its sheet or rule may no longer exist.
numberOrFormula: Enter a number or a formula starting with =
protected: This sheet is protected. Unprotect it before changing conditional formatting.
rangeOnSheet: Enter a range on this sheet
scaleHint: Leave thresholds blank for automatic values, or enter a number or a formula starting with =. Threshold formulas use fixed sheet references.
title: Conditional formatting
unknownKind: A rule of the kind "{kind}", which this version cannot edit
